title: Emission-fragment tracehook adapter and token-cost reconciler
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: instrument the inference path to emit per-emission-fragment (token/subtoken) traces and metrics that attribute latency and cost to the smallest observable unit while accounting for cache (prefix/KV) effects. Deliverables: a lightweight tracehook adapter in the serving runtime, a token event schema for ingestion, aggregation rules for KV-hit adjusted latency and cost, and dashboard panels in Console that expose token-level hotspots and cache-sensitivity insights.

Scope and boundaries:
- Capture micro-timings for discrete stages: tokenization, prefetch/KV lookup, kernel execution, emit serialization, and post-processing.
- Record cache signals (kv_hit boolean, prefetch_origin) to enable delta-attribution when a cache hit bypasses work.
- Avoid storing raw token text for persisted traces; use deterministic token hashes for joinability while meeting privacy requirements.
- Use sampling to limit volume: deterministic sampling keys for controlled customers, 5% uniform sampling for public tenants, and full-capture for requests that exceed latency or error thresholds.

Telemetry schema (proposal):
- token.event_version = "v1"
- token.span_id = string(token-span-uuid)
- token.index = integer as string
- token.hash = sha256_hex(token_text)
- token.kv_hit = "true" | "false"
- token.stage_latency_ms = list of stage timings as comma-separated string: "tokenize,kv_lookup,kernel,emit,postproc"
- token.total_latency_ms = integer as string
- token.kernel_offload_ms = integer as string
- token.batch_size_at_emit = integer as string
- token.request_tier = "hosted" | "dedicated" | "private"
- token.sampling_reason = "uniform-5pct" | "deterministic-user" | "latency-trigger"

Storage and aggregation plan:
- Structured log event emitted from runtime to ingestion (JSON-L), routed to the token-events topic in our metrics pipeline.
- Short-term store: ClickHouse table partitioned by day and customer. Columns are flattened strings (no nested JSON) to match pipeline constraints.
- Aggregates: Prometheus-style metrics emitted via push gateway for histograms (token.total_latency_ms buckets) and counters for kv_hit vs kv_miss. Aggregation jobs compute kv-adjusted per-token cost model (taking kernel_ms and whether kv_hit) nightly for cost reconciliation.

Dashboard and alerting:
- Console panels:
  * Token latency heatmap: percentile distribution of token.total_latency_ms by token.hash for high-volume keys.
  * KV sensitivity view: top token hashes where kv_miss causes >X ms increase in median latency.
  * Cost delta chart: projected per-token cost change when toggling caching/quantization for model variants.
- Alerts: SLO breach if 95th token latency increases by >10% week-over-week for any model route.

Implementation phases:
1) Runtime shim (canary): add TraceHookAdapter that attaches token-level spans with minimal allocation; produce JSON-L events to local test topic. (owner: Miguel)
2) Ingestion pipeline mapping: create token-events topic schema, ClickHouse mapping, and aggregation job skeleton. (owner: Data Infra)
3) SDK/trace propagation: ensure trace context and request_id propagate from API layer to runtime so token spans can be correlated to requests. (owner: Backend SDK)
4) Dashboard queries and panels: Console team implements visualization and RBAC controls for token-level views. (owner: Console)
5) Rollout and opt-in controls: expose sampling knobs per-customer in Console; default to conservative sampling.

Privacy and security considerations:
- Do not persist raw token text. Persist only token.hash and token_length as integers.
- Token hashes are salted per-customer to reduce cross-tenant correlation; salt rotates every 90 days.
- Retention: raw token-event rows TTL=30 days, aggregates retained 365 days.
- Security review required because token hashes are derived from user data and will be stored; KMS usage for salt keys.

Testing strategy:
- Unit: validate TraceHookAdapter emits expected fields and sampling flags.
- Integration: runtime -> local ingestion -> ClickHouse end-to-end with synthetic requests covering cache hit/miss scenarios.
- Load: synthetic high-throughput test to validate sampling backpressure and verify no >5% RPS impact on serving latency when adapter is enabled.

Rollout and runbook:
- Canary 1: 1% of traffic on an internal staging org for 48 hours, monitor overhead and errors.
- Canary 2: 5% uniform sampling across hosted with telemetry validation.
- Enable full sampling for selected enterprise customers by request.
- Runbook notes: disable adapter via runtime feature flag if production CPU overhead >2% or if token-events pipeline becomes saturated.

Success criteria:
- Instrumentation adds <2% p50 overhead to serving latency in canary traffic.
- Token-events ingestion sustains 10k token events/sec on the pipeline at steady state with configured sampling.
- Dashboards surface actionable hotspots and the cost-reconciler job produces per-model delta reports used by Optimize recommendations.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- How to attribute shared kernel time across concurrent tokens in a batched emit: heuristics (pro-rata by token-length) vs advanced causal tracing.
- Volume: whether 5% uniform sampling is sufficient to detect regressions for long-tail tokens.
- Token hashing vs token fingerprinting (we prefer salted hash to reduce privacy risk).
